Cobalt (Co) metallization presents a promising alternative strategy for the bottom interconnect in advanced chip manufacture, yet
the interfacial structure and functionality ofan organic additive essential for superconformal Co deposition is far from clear given
the concurring hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein, interfacial electrochemistry for a model additive molecule MBIS
(sodium 2-mercapto-5-benzimidazolesulfonate) at a Co electrode is investigated by applying in situ surface-enhanced infrared
absorption spectroscopy and electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance combined with density functional theory calculations
The vertical plane adsorption of MBIS on the Co surface via thiolate reduces the overall reduction current with a higher/lower
Faradaic efficiency (FE) towards HER/Co deposition due to the significant blockage of surface Co sites as well as the formation
of Co(II) complex with MBIS. Surface coverage of MBIS is found to decrease with increasing pH and overpotential, which may
account for the location-dependent functionality of MBIS in practical Co deposition in vias. This work provides a molecular-
level insight into the interfacial mechanism of an organic additive essential for the Co superfilling scenario.

Notably, despite their significant achievement from a si-
mulation perspective, these models lack a molecular-level
insight into the interaction of a specific organic additive with
a Co electrode as well as its impact on the Co electro-
deposition, which is otherwise highly demanded for the
mechanistic understanding and design ofadvanced additives.
Along this line, in situ surface molecular spectroscopies are
expected to be valuable for this purpose. The use of surface
Raman spectroscopy is limited owing to the very low SERS
activity at Co surfaces and the very difficult optical focusing
with the strong HER condition. This challenge can be well
addressed by the application of the in situ ATR-SEIRAS
technique which is least metal-specific and free of gas evo-
lution concern [32–40]. Besides, the convincing analysis of
ATR-SEIRAS results towards the assignment of vibrational
peaks and the determination of adsorption geometries calls
for supplemental support of relevant density functional the-
ory (DFT) calculations.
In this work, MBIS, an organic additive already validated
for nano-vias Co superfilling [14], is selected as the target
model molecule. The interfacial structure and mechanistic
aspect of adsorbed MBIS at the Co electrode are probed
initially by high sensitivity in situ ATR-SEIRAS and DFT
calculations. Electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance
(EQCM) is applied to quantify the relative contributions of
Co deposition and HER in the Co-plating solutions with and
without the additive. Potential and pH dependencies of
MBIS on Co deposition rates provide an inference to the
interfacial functionality of MBIS in Co superfilling.

3 Conclusions
In this study, we have delved into the inhibition mechanism
of the additive MBIS in acidic Co electroplating using a
synergistic approach inclusive of electrochemical and ATR-
SEIRAS measurement as well as computational simulations.
The MBIS molecule adapts a nearly vertical adsorption
configuration on the Co electrode via the formation of
thiolate, reducing both partial currents for Co deposition and
\mathrm { H } _ { 2 }
evolution with a higher
\mathrm { F E } _ { \mathrm { C o } }
and a lower
\mathrm { F E } _ { \mathrm { H } _ { 2 } } ,
, as
compared to the MBIS-free case. We have revealed at a
molecular level that the adsorbed MBIS molecules disrupt
the hydrogen bonding of interfacial water, and form a sort of
interfacial
\mathrm { M B I S - C o } ^ { \overline { { 2 } } + }
complex, thereby favoring a higher
selectivity toward the hydrogen evolution than the Co de-
position. Furthermore, variation in the MBIS coverage has
been identified with varying pHs or potentials, offering
crucial insights into the refinement of electroplating para-
meters. The MBIS coverage-dependent inhibition effect can
qualitatively account for the Co superfilling process. Our
work is valuable in understanding the interfacial structure
and functionality of a typical inhibitor for superconformal
Co plating and lends important guidance for filling simula-
tions.

crucial insights into the refinement of electroplating para-
meters. The MBIS coverage-dependent inhibition effect can
qualitatively account for the Co superfilling process. Our
work is valuable in understanding the interfacial structure
and functionality of a typical inhibitor for superconformal
Co plating and lends important guidance for filling simula-
tions.
